findings.title: Installed H1 permalink separator makes valid rendered headings fail

source_proof.details: linkInsideHeader defaults space:true and placement:after. Its implementation pushes a separate text token containing one U+0020 before pushing the permalink anchor. VitePress configures symbol and renderAttrs without overriding space. The complete frozen config has no anchor override.

findings.failure: Node.text(omit_permalink=True) suppresses the anchor node but retains its preceding sibling space. All 39 manifest H1 values end without that separator. The first otherwise-valid reader therefore fails the exact H1 comparison. The scaffold concatenates heading and anchor without the installed separator, masking the mismatch.
findings.required_change: Bind the exact installed permalink separator representation in expectations or validate and remove only that source-defined separator when extracting the heading. Preserve exact heading-content comparison and the Appendix F inline-code distinction. Make the synthetic positive fixture include the real separator, with negative controls for changed heading content and an extra separator. Do not broadly strip heading whitespace.

completed_checks.result: Read every function and CLI path in both files, plus complete packet README, preparation script, build/check caller and verification request. Runner allocation and process-ownership implementation remain outside this bounded checker review.

All 39 source hashes independently match git show a3e4c29:path. All 39 frontmatter titles, raw H1 values and all 247 complete language/raw-fence pairs independently match. All source bodies use LF without CR. Independent multiline Markdown-link extraction matches all 247 target/fragment pairs.

Installed highlighter calls trimEnd once on the whole fence. ECMAScript suffix set matches the checker; no linewise trim or tab expansion. Installed Shiki classic structure joins line spans with LF and empty-line wbr contributes no text. Current languages asm/json/sh/text need no Vue mustache restoration; notation directives are excluded. Raw and rendered identities remain separate.

Read complete installed sidebar, group, item, VPDoc, VPDocFooter, VPLink and prev-next sources, plus link normalization and configured theme. Sidebar direct headers/items match the checker shape. Flattened chapter/appendix order matches the manifest. Unlisted index lookup index=-1 gives next=chapter01 and no previous. Appendix F visible code text omits backticks while literal frontmatter browser/sidebar text retains them. H1 separator exception is the finding above.

39 reader HTML paths required; extra HTML outside framework 404 and the single public passthrough rejected. The 321-byte public passthrough is exact-byte/hash evidence only. Editorial subtree and symlinks rejected. Framework 404 is excluded rather than semantically accepted.

All 33 retained on-disk receipts match their embedded JSON and SHA-256. Every retained after-tree HTML entry matches its actual file hash. Reviewed each control mutation and reported first failure. Positive receipts count 39 documents/247 links/45 fragments/39 sidebars/39 pagers/247 fences/one passthrough. Existing receipt refusal exits 2 and preserves its original bytes. Mismatch/input/internal exceptions become failure; successful checker exit requires passed status; build failure skips validation. Interrupted running receipts cannot count as passed.

remaining_limits: No real HTML output has been built or inspected. H1 source-contract correction is independently clear; synthetic controls do not establish real emitted output or allocate a build.

The synthetic baseline derives expected links, fences and labels from the same manifest. Independent frozen-source comparisons reduce that shared-oracle risk but do not establish real emitted DOM correctness.

Document links are compared as a target/fragment multiset, not bound to visible labels or source positions. Swapping two destination attributes can preserve that multiset. This does not invalidate the narrower resolution/count check, and no claim of label-to-destination preservation is made.

HTMLParser plus explicit structural checks is not a complete browser HTML conformance validator. CSS visibility, script behaviour, hydration, layout, accessibility, browser interaction, global site and publication remain unaccepted.
Source identity and synthetic mutation detection do not prove inherited reader claims, historical runtime results or physical hardware behaviour.

h1_bounded_confirmation.scope: Complete changed H1 extraction/validation code and every changed scaffold/control mutation, with actual retained receipt and after-tree identities. No repeat of the old whole review.

checks: The one header-anchor is the final direct child of the sole scoped H1. A nested or additional header-anchor cannot satisfy that final direct-child identity.

The heading has a nonempty id. The permalink is an a element with exactly class=header-anchor, href=# plus that id and aria-label=Permalink to followed by the quoted raw source_h1. Appendix F backticks remain in this attribute.
The permalink has exactly one decoded U+200B child, with no nested markup or extra symbol text.

All prefix children are decoded without whitespace normalization and compared with the visible H1 plus exactly one U+0020. Missing, extra or tab separators fail. Ordinary content and Appendix F inline-code text remain exact.
Node.text no longer offers arbitrary header-anchor suppression. Title/sidebar/code paths keep their ordinary decoded text extraction.

h1_bounded_confirmation.scaffold_readback: The baseline now emits the exact U+0020, direct final anchor, self-id href, escaped raw-source aria-label and numeric U+200B entity.
